collect._url_comment: Every page the nav offers plus every product page. The list once stopped at five and left several pages ungated, so a product could ship with a failing accessibility or SEO score. A URL added here must already build on the branch that adds it: this same file is what .github/workflows/pr-ci.yml feeds Lighthouse on EVERY pull request, and `lhci collect` exits 1 on a 404, so listing a page before it exists reds the whole wave. Add the URL in the PR that adds the page, and DELETE it in the PR that removes the page — a retired page left here reds the run just as hard as one that never existed.
collect._output_comment: No setting in this file can move lhci's output out of the repo — .gitignore is the mitigation, not a stopgap someone should keep trying to replace. Checked in @lhci/cli@0.15.1 rather than assumed: reports go to a module constant, path.join(process.cwd(), '.lighthouseci') in @lhci/utils/src/saved-reports.js, and collect.js calls saveLHR(lhr) with no directory argument; upload.outputDir is documented '[filesystem only]' and this config uploads to temporary-public-storage. Chrome's profile directory is equally out of reach: lighthouse's getDebuggableChrome (cli/run.js) hands chrome-launcher only port, ignoreDefaultFlags, chromeFlags and logLevel, and chrome-launcher creates its own temp profile before Chrome reads a single flag — under WSL that lands in the repo root, which is what .gitignore's backslash and undefined: patterns catch. Adding --user-data-dir, --crash-dumps-dir and --disk-cache-dir to chromeFlags below produces byte-identical litter and never creates the /tmp target it names, so do not add them back.
collect._chromeflags_comment: chromeFlags is a space-separated STRING, never a JSON array. @lhci/cli@0.15.1's collect/node-runner.js:47-49 does `let s = chromeFlags || ''; s += ' --headless=new'`, and `+=` stringifies an array by comma-join, so the array form reached Chrome as one bogus switch, `--no-sandbox,--headless,--disable-gpu`. Chrome ignores an unknown switch silently: running that single token alone dies with `Missing X server or $DISPLAY`, proving --headless — and with it --no-sandbox and --disable-gpu — never took effect. lighthouse@12.6.1's cli/run.js:33-63 re-splits the string with yargs-parser before handing it to chrome-launcher, so the string form delivers all three. --headless is kept here for intent even though lhci appends its own --headless=new; yargs merges the pair into --headless=true,new, which Chrome resolves to new headless (verified launching).

assert._matrix_comment: Two rows. Site pages keep every category. The generated Driftless demo bundle (static/demo/driftless/, emitted by svc-driftless bin/driftless-showcase.py with <meta name="robots" content="noindex, nofollow"> on purpose, line ~125) can never pass the SEO category: Lighthouse's is-crawlable audit fails by design and drags the score to ~0.54 (PR #345 CI, 2026-09-04). SEO is therefore not asserted there; accessibility stays an error at the same floor as the rest of the site, which is what the demo gate exists for.
